text: Let $A$ and $B$ be matrices of order $3\times 3$. If $|A| = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ and $|B| = \dfrac{1}{729}$, then what is the value of $\left|2B\,(\mathrm{adj}(3A))\right|$?
solution: $|2B\cdot\mathrm{adj}(3A)| = |2B|\cdot|\mathrm{adj}(3A)|$. For a $3\times3$ matrix, $|kM| = k^{3}|M|$ and $|\mathrm{adj}(M)| = |M|^{2}$. So $|2B| = 2^{3}|B| = 8\cdot\frac{1}{729}$, and $|\mathrm{adj}(3A)| = |3A|^{2} = (3^{3}|A|)^{2} = 729^{2}|A|^{2} \cdot \frac{1}{729}\,$... combining: $8\cdot\frac{1}{729}\cdot 729\,|A|^{2} = 8|A|^{2}$. With $|A| = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$, $|A|^{2} = \frac{1}{8}$, giving $8\cdot\frac{1}{8} = 1$.

text: If \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), then the inverse of \(\left(2A^2 + 5A\right)\) is
solution: \(A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & -5 \\ -5 & 10 \end{bmatrix}\). So \(2A^2 + 5A = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & -10 \\ -10 & 20 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 10 & -5 \\ -5 & 15 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 20 & -15 \\ -15 & 35 \end{bmatrix}\). Its determinant is \(20\cdot 35 - (-15)(-15) = 700 - 225 = 475\). Hence \((2A^2+5A)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{475}\begin{bmatrix} 35 & 15 \\ 15 & 20 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{95}\begin{bmatrix} 7 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\), which is option A.

text: Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&3\\1&-2&1\end{bmatrix},\ B=\begin{bmatrix}6\\11\\0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(X=\begin{bmatrix}a\\b\\c\end{bmatrix}\), if \(AX=B\), then the value of \(2a+b+2c\) is
solution: \(AX=B\) gives the system \(a+b+c=6\) ...(i), \(b+3c=11\) ...(ii), \(a-2b+c=0\) ...(iii). From (iii), \(a+c=2b\); substituting into (i): \(2b+b=6\Rightarrow b=2\). From (ii): \(c=3\). From (i): \(a=1\). Hence \(2a+b+2c=2(1)+2+2(3)=10\).

At \(x = \sqrt{2}\) both numerator and denominator vanish (a \(0/0\) form). Factor: \(x^{4} - 4 = (x^{2} - 2)(x^{2} + 2) = (x - \sqrt{2})(x + \sqrt{2})(x^{2} + 2)\) and \(x^{2} + 3\sqrt{2}\,x - 8 = (x - \sqrt{2})(x + 4\sqrt{2})\). Cancel \((x - \sqrt{2})\): \(\lim_{x \to \sqrt{2}} \dfrac{(x + \sqrt{2})(x^{2} + 2)}{x + 4\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{(2\sqrt{2})(4)}{5\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{5\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{8}{5}\).

text: If \(f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\sin^{3}(\sqrt{x}) \cdot \log(1 + 3x)}{\left(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}\right)^{2}\left(e^{5\sqrt{x}} - 1\right)x} & x \neq 0 \\ a & x = 0 \end{cases}\) is continuous in \([0,1]\), then \(a\) equals
solution: Continuity at \(0\) requires \(a = \lim_{x \to 0} f(x)\). Use the standard limits as \(x \to 0\): \(\sin^{3}\sqrt{x} \sim (\sqrt{x})^{3} = x^{3/2}\), \(\left(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}\right)^{2} \sim x\), \(\log(1 + 3x) \sim 3x\), \(e^{5\sqrt{x}} - 1 \sim 5\sqrt{x}\). Then \(a = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x^{3/2} \cdot 3x}{x \cdot x \cdot 5\sqrt{x}} = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{3x^{5/2}}{5x^{5/2}} = \dfrac{3}{5}\).
